newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary to allow alternative telecom network.
newsitem.headline: Hungary to allow alternative telecom network.

text.p: THe Hungarian government said on Thursday it plans to allow alternative telecommunications networks but was not considering bringing forward the end of national operator Matav's existing monopoly from 2001.
"An alternative telecommunications network is necessary," government spokesman Elemer Kiss told a news conference following Thursday's government meeting.

He added the government would authorise national rail company Magyar Allamvasutak Rt (MAV) to use its optical fibre trunk network as a contribution in kind to a future joint venture but can only do so after an open competition.
"The Transport Ministry has been authorised to immediately issue a tender."

MAV, MOL, electricity supplier MVM, the Hungarian post, and a number of smaller companies earlier signed a letter of intent to set up Pantel Rt, a consortium with pan-european telecom company Unisource.

MAV is to have a majority stake in the consortium, while Unisource -- an alliance of PTT Telecom of the Netherlands, the Swiss national operator and Sweden's Teila -- would keep all the management rights.

In a separate development, the government has also decided that the state should retain at least a 50 percent plus one share stake in national broadcaster Antenna Hungaria Rt (AH) and bring it "into a position to enter the telecommunications market" before privatisation.
Hungary's long-distance and international telephony is under the monopoly of Matav Rt, 67 percent owned by a 50-50 consortium of Ameritech and Deutsche Telekom, until the end of the year 2001.

AH has already started building a nationwide optical trunk network, to replace its ageing microwave communications system and plans to use part of its spare capacity to enter communications sectors which do not fall under the monopoly.
AH officials said earlier they might form some sort of partnership with companies such as MVM, MOL or MAV.
